notes: 'inventory_exclude_ip_prefixes' lists server ip prefixes the inventory pages leave out. It was a constant in dbabrain/lib/inventory_render.py until 2026-08-21, which meant the rendering library itself decided which of this estate's machines nobody gets to see. Empty means show everything.

Every 'time_window' hour and day bound is read in the timezone DBA Brain runs in - the 'timezone' field in config.json - on every node, whatever clock the host or container keeps. So 'from_hour': 1 is 01:00 there, not 01:00 UTC and not 01:00 on the machine. There is no per-entry timezone: one declaration decides every window in every file. Changing it moves every schedule that names an hour, so set it before the first scheduled run.

reports.note: Moved from the app command APP-REPORTS-INVENTORY-WORKFLOW by upgrade-config (0.22.0): the inventory is a report, built by the reports app's own pass.

availability.label: Availability
availability.note: If this is red the server is down or a database is not usable — nothing else matters first.

cpu.label: CPU
cpu.threshold: WARN ≥ 80% · CRITICAL ≥ 90% — the collector's severity, held for half of the last hour; the value is the hour's average
cpu.note: Sustained high CPU makes every query slower; check the top process and the heaviest queries. One sample at 95% is a moment, so the tile reads the hour (2026-10-26).

memory.label: Memory
memory.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used (report rule, on the last hour's average)
memory.note: A host short of memory swaps, and an engine short of cache reads the same pages from disk again and again.

sqlserver.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used · PLE < 2000 s = pressure (report rule, on the last hour's average)
sqlserver.note: Low page life expectancy means the buffer pool is churning: pages are read from disk again and again.

disk_space.label: Disk space
disk_space.threshold: host: WARN ≥ 85% used · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used; the engine's own files by its collector's rule
disk_space.note: A full data or log volume stops writes: the database goes read-only or the instance stalls.

sqlserver.threshold: host: WARN ≥ 85% used · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used; SQL Server: WARN < 10% or 10 GB free · CRITICAL < 5% or 5 GB free

disk_latency.label: Disk latency
disk_latency.threshold: WARN ≥ 20 ms · CRITICAL ≥ 50 ms — report rule, the collector logs only. Over the last hour, from the stored counters
disk_latency.note: Latency above ~20 ms per I/O means storage, not SQL, is the bottleneck. Graded on the last hour, from the file counters the store keeps; the latest interval and the last 24 hours are printed beside it, and the average since the engine started is printed and not graded.

storage_activity.label: Storage activity
storage_activity.threshold: WARN queue length ≥ 2 per spindle, held for half of the last hour — throughput and IOPS are logged, not judged
storage_activity.note: How hard the storage is being worked. A high queue with low throughput is a storage limit; high throughput on its own is just a busy server.

blocking.label: Blocking
blocking.threshold: WARN any blocked session · CRITICAL ≥ 10 blocked or blocked ≥ 300 s
blocking.note: One session holding a lock can stall an application entirely; find the head blocker.

long_queries.label: Long-running queries
long_queries.note: A query running for an hour is usually a missing index, a bad plan, or a runaway job.

backup.label: Backup
backup.threshold: per-database policy: required FULL/DIFF/LOG age from data/backup_policy.json
backup.note: Backup age is your worst-case data loss. A stale log backup means point-in-time recovery is not possible for that database.

jobs.label: Failed jobs
jobs.threshold: WARN any job failed since the last run
jobs.note: A failed maintenance job is a backup, an index rebuild or a purge that silently did not happen.

tempdb.label: Temporary space
tempdb.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% used and < 2 GB free · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used and < 1 GB free
tempdb.note: Temporary space filling up fails sorts and hashes — often a single bad query.

sqlserver.label: TempDB
sqlserver.note: TempDB filling up fails sorts, hashes and version store — often a single bad query.

security.label: Security
security.threshold: no sustained failed logins · no password older than the collector's threshold · no certificate expiring
security.note: Thousands of failed logins a day is a credential being guessed or an integration retrying a dead one — and it fills the error log either way.

ha.label: HA / replication
ha.threshold: every replica CONNECTED and SYNCHRONIZED / streaming
ha.note: A replica that stopped synchronising is not a replica: failover would lose data.

sqlserver.note: A replica that stopped synchronising is not a replica: failover would lose data. AVAILABILITY_DATABASE_HEALTH reads Availability Groups, database mirroring and log shipping (2008 R2 too, since 0.30.0) — on a Failover Cluster Instance with none of them it reports NOT_CONFIGURED, which is not an FCI health verdict.

oracle_processes.label: Sessions and processes
oracle_processes.threshold: WARN ≥ 80% of the processes / sessions limit · CRITICAL ≥ 90% — dead weight: WARN ≥ 10% of the process limit held by killed sessions or orphaned threads · CRITICAL ≥ 20%
oracle_processes.note: At the limit Oracle refuses every new connection (ORA-00020). A killed session or a thread with no session still holds its slot, so the ceiling can be reached by sessions that do no work.

oracle_tablespaces.label: Tablespaces
oracle_tablespaces.threshold: free space counting autoextend: WARN < 500 MB or < 5% · CRITICAL < 100 MB or < 2% — a segment at ≥ 90% of its extent limit is CRITICAL
oracle_tablespaces.note: A tablespace with no room fails the next insert into anything stored in it (ORA-01653); a segment at its extent limit fails the same way with space to spare.

oracle_sga.label: SGA memory
oracle_sga.threshold: shared pool free: WARN < 25 MB · CRITICAL < 10 MB — buffer cache hit ratio: WARN < 90%
oracle_sga.note: A shared pool with nothing free ends in ORA-04031: statements can no longer be parsed. A low buffer cache hit ratio means blocks are read from disk again and again.

oracle_rollback.label: Rollback segments
oracle_rollback.note: Transactions queueing for a rollback segment header: there are too few segments for the number of concurrent writers.

oracle_objects.label: Invalid objects
oracle_objects.threshold: WARN any invalid object · CRITICAL any unusable index
oracle_objects.note: Invalid code raises ORA-04068 when it is called, not when it broke; an unusable index fails every DML on its table unless SKIP_UNUSABLE_INDEXES is on.

postgres_wraparound.label: Transaction ID wraparound
postgres_wraparound.threshold: XID age: WARN ≥ 75% of autovacuum_freeze_max_age · CRITICAL ≥ 90%
postgres_wraparound.note: Past the freeze horizon PostgreSQL forces an aggressive vacuum, and at the hard limit it stops accepting writes until one finishes. The oldest database decides.

postgres_vacuum.label: Vacuum and bloat
postgres_vacuum.threshold: dead tuples in one table: WARN ≥ 100,000 · CRITICAL ≥ 1,000,000 — bloat: WARN any table ≥ 20% dead with over 10,000 rows · CRITICAL ≥ 40%
postgres_vacuum.note: Dead tuples are space vacuum has not reclaimed: scans read them and indexes point at them. A table that keeps growing here is one autovacuum cannot keep up with.

postgres_transactions.label: Long transactions
postgres_transactions.threshold: a transaction open: WARN ≥ 5 minutes · CRITICAL ≥ 30 minutes
postgres_transactions.note: An open transaction holds back vacuum for the whole cluster and keeps its locks; idle in transaction is the usual culprit.

postgres_indexes.label: Invalid indexes
postgres_indexes.threshold: CRITICAL any index left invalid or not ready
postgres_indexes.note: An invalid index is what a failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY leaves behind: it is maintained on every write and used by no query. Drop it and build it again.

metrics_failing.title: Metrics currently failing on {count} server(s)
metrics_failing.body: The newest run of these metrics did not return a usable result, so whatever the page shows for them is the last value from before they broke: {servers}.
metrics_failing.action: Read the collector error on the server page, then fix the credential, permission or connectivity behind it. Until it returns, treat that area as unknown, not healthy.

metrics_overdue.title: Metrics overdue on {count} server(s)
metrics_overdue.body: No attempt for at least three of the metric's own intervals: {servers}.
metrics_overdue.action: Check the scheduler and the metric's time_window; a windowed metric outside its hours is expected, a five-minute metric hours behind is not.

metrics_no_evidence.title: Catalog metrics with no evidence on {count} server(s)
metrics_no_evidence.body: Active in the metric catalog for this engine but no rows in the window — either never collected here, or switched off for this target: {servers}.
metrics_no_evidence.action: Confirm each is deliberately disabled (metrics.metric_overrides in db_instances.json). Anything not deliberately off is a monitoring blind spot, not a healthy signal.

stale_servers.title: {count} server(s) show last known values, not current ones
stale_servers.body: Nothing was collected from these recently, so none of their figures is graded here: {servers}.
stale_servers.action: Bring collection back (metrics switched off, a login or host access lost), or take the server off the report.

services_stopped.title: {count} monitored service(s) are not running
services_stopped.body: A service the host is monitored for is stopped or missing: {servers}. On an application host this is the workload itself being down.
services_stopped.action: {metric_action} If the name is wrong, fix OS_SERVICE_NAMES for that target.

log_rpo_violated.title: Transaction-log RPO violated on {count} server(s)
log_rpo_violated.body: The newest LOG backup is past the RPO these databases are held to: {servers}. Point-in-time recovery is unavailable for the period since that backup. Whether the log *chain* is intact is a separate question: it needs backup LSN and recovery-fork evidence, which is not collected.
log_rpo_violated.action: Check the LOG backup job, its destination and its credentials, and confirm no database silently switched to SIMPLE. Verify LSN continuity before deciding a fresh FULL is required — taking one when the chain was intact discards a working restore path.

backup_not_graded.title: Backup compliance is not being graded on {count} server(s)
backup_not_graded.body: Backup evidence was collected and there is no policy to judge it against — data/backup_policy.json is absent on this node, or carries no rule: {servers}{more}. These read Unverified rather than Compliant, and no RPO or backup-age finding on them can appear anywhere on this page. Until 2026-09-14 they read '15/15 DB within policy' instead.
backup_not_graded.action: Restore data/backup_policy.json on this node — 'dbabrain init' writes the shipped default, and a node configured from a bundle gets the estate's own copy. Then re-run the inventory workflow and read the Backup column again before trusting any 'OK' on it.

backup_aging.title: Backups approaching their policy limit on {count} server(s)
backup_aging.action: Check the schedule before the next run misses; confirm the job is enabled.

not_inventoried.title: {count} target(s) cannot be fully inventoried (auth / connectivity)
not_inventoried.body: Backup and health posture is unverifiable on: {servers}. These are blind spots, not confirmed-healthy.
not_inventoried.action: Fix monitoring credentials / firewall / legacy client so collection succeeds; re-run before trusting any 'OK'.

no_log_requirement.title: {count} server(s) have no LOG backup requirement
no_log_requirement.body: Policy requires no transaction-log backup on: {servers}. Worst-case data loss is a whole FULL cycle.
no_log_requirement.action: Confirm the recovery model is deliberately SIMPLE. If it is not, move the databases to FULL recovery and schedule log backups.

failed_logins.title: Failed logins on {count} server(s)
failed_logins.body: Principals failing to authenticate, as the collector flags them: {servers}. Either the credential is being guessed, or an integration is retrying a dead one, and the error log is being filled either way.
failed_logins.action: Identify the source host of the attempts, then disable/fix the principal or block the source. Do not simply raise the alert threshold.

passwords_old.title: SQL logins with old passwords
passwords_old.action: Rotate the service logins on a schedule; start with sa and anything with db_owner.

low_ple.title: Memory pressure — low PLE under session load
low_ple.body: Page Life Expectancy is low (buffer pool churning) on: {servers}.
low_ple.action: Review max server memory vs. host RAM, top missing indexes, plan-cache bloat (enable optimize-for-ad-hoc).

disk_critical.title: Disk critically low (near full) on {count} volume(s)
disk_critical.body: Volumes at/near 0% free — imminent risk of data/log write failure: {detail}.
disk_critical.action: Free space / extend the volume now; archive old backups.

disk_low.title: Low disk headroom on production volumes
disk_low.body: Approaching the danger zone for data/log growth: {detail}.
disk_low.action: Plan capacity / archive old backups; set disk alerts at 15%.

wrong_edition.title: {count} production instance(s) on an edition not meant for production
wrong_edition.action: Move the instance to a licensed production edition, or correct its environment in the inventory if it is not production.

not_encrypted.title: Data files not encrypted at rest on {count} server(s)
not_encrypted.body: A copy of these files opens on another install, so whoever is an administrator on the host can take the data: {servers}.
not_encrypted.action: Detection only: each server's page lists the databases, who the host's administrators are, and the engine's way to encrypt.

xp_cmdshell.title: Security — xp_cmdshell enabled
xp_cmdshell.body: xp_cmdshell is ON for: {servers}. Often needed by legacy jobs but widens the attack surface.
xp_cmdshell.action: Confirm intentional / scope it; otherwise disable.

no_dr.title: No documented HA/DR for standalone production
no_dr.body: Core data on standalone servers without a documented DR strategy: {servers}.
no_dr.action: Document or stand up a DR strategy for these servers.

inventory_notes.title: Documented inventory notes (not live measurements)
inventory_notes.body: Recorded in the inventory (incl. hosts without live DB metrics): {detail}.
inventory_notes.action: Review each; fix collection where a finding is 'not connected'.

config_drift.title: Fleet-wide config baseline drift (quick wins)
config_drift.body: Across {count} server(s): backup compression OFF, remote DAC OFF, optimize-for-ad-hoc OFF, blocked-process-threshold 0, and/or cost-threshold-for-parallelism at the default 5.
config_drift.action: Apply a documented SQL config baseline via script; re-scan to confirm.
